notes: The judged intents the tool-search case file is generated from. Each intent is written twice (zh / en) and pairs the two forms, so the report's pair table answers the only question that matters for a multilingual gate: does the SAME intent move the probability when the language changes. `expect` is the tool that directly does the job; `distract` are near-misses — same domain, different action (query vs describe vs list, navigate vs snapshot) — because a distractor that is obviously unrelated calibrates nothing. The no_tool arm is where a false positive costs the most: the right answer there is 'no tool', and any tool the gate lets through is a wrong tool offered to the model.
